note: Original factual annotations. Event URLs cite dates and claims; coordinates locate the named place approximately, not battlefield boundaries. BC dates use astronomical years (1 BC = 0).

items.title: Hadrian’s Wall: west
items.text: Bowness-on-Solway marks the western end of the wall begun after Hadrian’s visit in AD 122.

items.title: Hadrian’s Wall: east
items.text: Wallsend marks the eastern end. Endpoint markers do not trace the wall’s surveyed course.

items.title: Antonine frontier
items.text: In the 140s Rome pushed north to the Forth–Clyde isthmus. AD 142 is the conventional start date, not an instantaneous completed line.
items.source: UNESCO, Frontiers of the Roman Empire

items.title: Rhine frontier
items.text: Rheinbrohl anchors the northern end of the Upper German–Raetian frontier, built in stages during the second century. AD 150 is a period anchor.
items.source: UNESCO, Frontiers of the Roman Empire

items.title: Danube frontier
items.text: Bad Gögging to Iža was a fortified river frontier; this point locates its western segment. AD 150 is a period anchor.
